Aerial Wildlife Survey Report  
Wildlife Management Units 436, 437, 438 and 439 Bighorn Sheep Survey (2019-2020) 
 
Background 
Aerial surveys of the Eastern Slopes of Alberta for bighorn sheep (Ovis canadensis) abundance, composition and 
location have been conducted since 1972. Since 1978, surveys have focused on “selected” winter ranges, where 
concentrations of bighorn sheep had been identified during previous flights. This report summarizes observations 
of bighorn sheep obtained during an aerial survey of selected winter ranges on January 21, 22, 23, 26, and 
Febrary 2, 18, 23 of 2020 in Widlife Mangement Units (WMU) 436, 437, 438 and 439. The obj ective of the survey 
was to document the abundance and composition of bighorn sheep. 
 
Trophy sheep (4/5 curl or greater) hunting opportunities in WMU 436 and 439 are general season hunts occurring 
between August 25 and October 31. In WMU 437 and 438-C Trophy hunting is manged through a limited entry 
hunt during set dates depending on the unit. Non-trophy hunting opportunies exist in WMU 437 and 438-A/C/D 
between September 10 and October 31, with generally low realized harvest rates.  
 
Survey Method 
A Bell 206 helicopter was used to survey each mountain complex and associated drainages for bighorn sheep and 
other ungulates. Each selected winter range was flown at an altitude between the treeline and the ridgetop (about 
5500-7000 feet above sea level), in an attempt to provide complete coverage of sheep habitat in each complex.  
On tall slopes, a high and a low pass were conducted to ensure full coverage by the survey crew.   
 
Sheep were classified according to sex (ewes or rams) and age (lambs or adults). All sheep over one year of age 
were considered adult (including long yearlings), while sheep under one year of age (short yearlings) were 
classified as lambs. Rams were further classified according to horn-size categories: ¼ curl, ½ curl, ¾ curl, or 4/5 
curl (legal). Unclassified sheep were either rams (horn size could not be determined) or could not be identified 
based on either sex or age. Other ungulates observed were also classified according to sex and age where 
possible. 
 
A total of 31 hours were flown between January 21 and February 23 2020.
